- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates mean-reversion strength; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.5) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.
- When sentiment is consistently negative and price is near support, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid bottoming too early.
